title: Canonical restrictions through the two Cartesian diagonal squares
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; absolute separatedness is not assumed. All morphisms below are separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Every smooth morphism below is assumed to have a pure relative dimension $d_h\geq0$. Work in the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$, take $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\simeq Ru^!Rv^!$ to be the specified adjunction conjugate of compact-support composition [def-pur-finite-exceptional-composition], and take $\theta_{h,M}$ and $\beta_{h,v}$ to be the specified counit transposes [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] put $\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\theta_{u,\omega_v}\mathrm{sym}$. All pullback compositions, tensor constraints and unit comparisons below are the canonical derived ones [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].
Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth of pure dimensions $d,e\geq0$. Set $Q=X\times_ZY$, $W=X\times_ZX$, and define $a(x,x')=(x,fx')$, $b(x,y)=x$, $l(x,x')=x'$, $r(x,y)=y$, $s(x)=(x,fx)$ and $t(x)=(x,x)$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The diagram with rows $W\xrightarrow aQ\xrightarrow bX$, $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ and vertical maps $l,r,gf$ has two Cartesian squares. The maps $a,b,ba$ are smooth separated finite type of dimensions $d,e,d+e$, and $at=s$, $lt=1$, $rs=f$, $ba=p_{gf}$.
For $h=f,g,gf$, let $W_h$ be its self-fibre product, $p_h$ its first projection, $\Delta_h$ its diagonal, $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant], and $\alpha_h:C_h\simeq\omega_h$ the specified inverse base-change restriction [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Define $i:W_f\to W$ by the same pair and $j:Q\to W_g$ by $(x,y)\mapsto(fx,y)$. The squares $(p_f,a,s,i)$ and $(b,p_g,f,j)$ are Cartesian, with $i\Delta_f=t$ and $js=\Delta_gf$. Put
$$A=\beta_{f,r},\quad B=\beta_{g,gf},\quad D=\beta_{gf,gf},\quad T_f=\beta_{a,s},\quad T_g=\beta_{p_g,f},$$
$$\gamma_f=L\Delta_f^*T_f^{-1}:C_f\simeq Lt^*\omega_a,\qquad\gamma_g=Ls^*T_g:Lf^*C_g\simeq Ls^*\omega_b.$$
Then the following identities hold for these specified maps:
$$\alpha_f=(Lt^*A)^{-1}\gamma_f,\qquad Lf^*\alpha_g=(Ls^*B)^{-1}\gamma_g,\qquad\alpha_{gf}=(Lt^*D)^{-1}.$$
No diagonal orientation or Tate-twist comparison is chosen.

source.place: Step 1, canonical twofold fibre-product identifications and diagonal base-change restrictions (old item steps 1 and 4); agent-written refinement of the blueprint argument

proof.text: Use the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] on arbitrary test schemes. A map to $W$ is a pair $(x,x')$ with $gf(x)=gf(x')$, and a map to $Q$ is $(x,y)$ with $gf(x)=g(y)$. Specifying $(x,y)$ and $x'$ with $y=f(x')$ is exactly specifying $(x,x')$; hence the square $(a,l;r,f)$ is Cartesian. Specifying $x$ and $y$ with $gf(x)=g(y)$ proves that $(b,r;gf,g)$ is Cartesian. For the square with $p_f,a,s,i$, the condition $a(x,x')=s(x)$ is exactly $f(x')=f(x)$, giving $W_f$. For the square with $b,p_g,f,j$, a pair $(y_1,y_2)$ over $Z$ with $y_1=f(x)$ is exactly $(x,y_2)\in Q$. These descriptions give mutually inverse maps by uniqueness, not just bijections on geometric points. Comparing their projections gives $at=s$, $lt=1$, $rs=f$, $ba=p_{gf}$, $i\Delta_f=t$, $js=\Delta_g\circ f$, and $li=p_{2,f}$, where $p_{2,f}:W_f\to X$ is the second projection.

source.place: Step 1: canonical twofold fibre-product identifications; explicit universal-property verification

proof.text: The first two squares exhibit $a$ as the base change of $f$ and $b$ as the base change of $g$. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] to obtain dimensions $d,e$ and dimension $d+e$ for $ba$, and also for $gf$. Separatedness and finite type of the base changes follow from [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; $gf$ is in the standing separated finite-type domain. The same arguments apply to the projections $p_f,p_g$, to $j$ (the base change of $f$ along $p_g$), and to $r,l$ (the base changes of $gf$ along $g$ and along $gf$). The remaining displayed maps are closed immersions: $bs=1_X$ and $p_{gf}t=1_X$ with $b,p_{gf}$ separated, so $s,t$ are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-from-composite]; likewise $\Delta_f,\Delta_g$; and $i$ is the base change of $s$ along $a$ in the Cartesian square $(p_f,a,s,i)$, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Closed immersions are separated and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a). Thus every arrow of the four Cartesian squares is separated and of finite type, as the cited exchange and pasting statements require.

source.place: Step 1: smoothness and dimensions of the twofold fibre-product projections; Stacks Tags 01VA, 01VB, 02NK, 02NL, 01KU, 01T4

proof.text: By [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], the specified maps $A,B,D,T_f,T_g$ are isomorphisms, including when their base maps $s,f$ are not smooth. For each smooth $h$ involved, [def-pur-co-smoothness] supplies the etale-origin witness of $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ and the invertible transported compact-support exchange at that object; hence the exchange inverses used below are on its stated witnessed finite-coefficient domain. By [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] and the specified direction of $\beta$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness], put $E_f=\beta_{f,f}$ and $E_g=\beta_{g,g}$. Then $\alpha_f=(L\Delta_f^*E_f)^{-1}$ and $\alpha_g=(L\Delta_g^*E_g)^{-1}$, under the section pullback identifications. All pullbacks below use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. In Lean, specialize the horizontal pasting clause to the etale monoidal unit. Its comparison image is constructible of finite Tor amplitude: the unit is constructible with Tor interval [0,0], and comparison preserves this property. Both successive pullbacks of the etale unit remain constructible of finite Tor amplitude, hence bounded below. The exceptional image under the last vertical arrow is bounded below, so [lem-weil-pbc-fixed-module-derived-hom-bijection] reflects the pro-etale pasting equality back to etale coordinates. Naturality of exceptional base change with respect to the pullback unit isomorphism and the unit equation of [lem-kun-derived-pullback-composition-monoidal] identify that specialization with the specified dualizing beta maps. The two section-composition calculations use associativity and identity coherence of the canonical derived etale pullback comparisons; mapping the resulting etale equalities by comparison gives exactly the three SameProEtaleMap clauses.

source.place: Step 1, final paragraph: the specified smooth-base-change restrictions, before any orientation

proof.text:
Paste the square for $A=\beta_{f,r}$ with its base change along $s:X\to Q$. Its outer square is the self-base-change square for $f$, since $rs=f$ and $li=p_{2,f}$. Apply the horizontal-pasting identity of [lem-pur-smooth-exceptional-tensor-pasting] with $h=f$, $v=r$, $w=s$, $u'=i$ and $N=\Lambda_Y$, whose unit values are the specified $\beta$ of [def-pur-co-smoothness]; consequently
$$E_f=T_f\circ Li^*A.$$
Concretely the transpose of the right side first applies the inverse exchange for $s$, then the pulled-back inverse exchange for $r$, then $Lf^*\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y}$; exchange pasting makes the first two arrows the inverse exchange for $rs=f$, so this is the defining transpose of $E_f$, and the cited identity is exactly this statement. Pull back along $\Delta_f$ and use $i\Delta_f=t$:
$$L\Delta_f^*E_f=(L\Delta_f^*T_f)\circ Lt^*A.$$
Taking inverses gives $\alpha_f=(Lt^*A)^{-1}\circ L\Delta_f^*T_f^{-1}=(Lt^*A)^{-1}\gamma_f$.

source.place: Step 1, final paragraph: base-change squares of the composite; first diagonal restriction, with the counit transpose expanded

proof.text:
Now paste the self-base-change square of $g$ with its base change along $f:X\to Y$. The latter square is $(b,p_g,f,j)$, and the outer square is the one for $B=\beta_{g,gf}$, since $p_{2,g}j=r$. The horizontal-pasting identity of [lem-pur-smooth-exceptional-tensor-pasting] with $h=g$, $v=g$, $w=f$, $u'=j$ and $N=\Lambda_Z$, read on unit values as above, gives
$$B=T_g\circ Lj^*E_g.$$
Indeed its transpose applies the inverse exchange for $f$, the pulled-back inverse exchange for $g$, and then $L(gf)^*\varepsilon_{g,\Lambda_Z}$; pasting gives the defining counit transpose of $B$ in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Pull back along $s$, and use $js=\Delta_g\circ f$ and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]:
$$Ls^*B=(Ls^*T_g)\circ Lf^*L\Delta_g^*E_g=\gamma_g\circ(Lf^*\alpha_g)^{-1}.$$
Multiplication by the inverses gives $Lf^*\alpha_g=(Ls^*B)^{-1}\gamma_g$.

source.place: Step 1, final paragraph: base-change squares of the composite; second diagonal restriction with the explicit pasting substitution

proof.text: For $h=gf$, the self-base-change comparison is $D=\beta_{gf,gf}$ and its diagonal is $t$. The specified inverse restriction of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change] is therefore $\alpha_{gf}=(Lt^*D)^{-1}$, using $lt=1$. Every displayed map was formed from pullbacks and the specified counit mates; none used an orientation or a Tate twist.

source.place: Step 1, final paragraph: restriction for the composite diagonal
